resolved.title: 字符串 String
resolved.description:
[s0l0!-header][h1]Strings[/h1][/s0l0!-header]

A [b]string[/b] in C is an array of characters that ends with a [b]NULL character '\0'[/b]. 
A string declaration can be made in several ways, each with its own considerations. 
[s0l0!-header][b]For example:[/b][/s0l0!-header] [code format="c" ]char str_name[str_len] = "string"; [/code]
This creates a string named [i]str_name[/i] of [i]str_len[/i] characters and initializes it to the value "string". 
When you provide a [b]string literal[/b] to initialize the string, the compiler automatically adds a NULL character '\0' to the char array.
For this reason, you must  declare the array size to be at least one character longer than the expected string length.
The statements below creates strings that include the NULL character. If the declaration does not include a char array size, then it will be calculated based on the length of the string in the initialization plus one for '\0': [code format="c" codeId="1741"]char str1[6] = "hello";
char str2[ ] = "world";  /* size 6 */[/code]
A string can also be declared as a set of characters: [code format="c" codeId="1742"]char str3[6] = {'h', 'e', 'l', 'l', 'o', '\0'};

char str4[ ] = {'h', 'e', 'l', 'l', 'o', '\0'}; /* size 6 */ [/code]
With this approach, the NULL character must be added explicitly. Note that the [b]characters[/b] are enclosed in single quotation marks.
As with any array, the name of a string acts as a [b]pointer[/b].
A string literal is a text enclosed in double quotation marks. 
A character, such as 'b', is indicated by single quotation marks and cannot be treated as a string.

A string pointer declaration such as char [b]*str = "stuff";[/b] is considered a constant and cannot be changed from its initial value. 

To safely and conveniently operate with strings, you can use the [i]Standard Library[/i] string functions shown below. Don't forget to include <string.h>.
[b]strlen[/b]() - get length of a string
[b]strcat[/b]() - merge two strings
[b]strcpy[/b]() - copy one string to another
[b]strlwr[/b]() - convert string to lower case
[b]strupr[/b]() - convert string to upper case
[b]strrev[/b]() - reverse string
[b]strcmp[/b]() - compare two strings
[note]String functions and string pointers are covered in later lessons.[/note]

content.text:
程序通常是交互式的，要求用户输入。
为了从用户那里获取一行文本或其他字符串，C提供了**scanf**()、**gets**()和**fgets**()函数。

你可以使用**scanf**()根据格式指定符来读取输入的字符串。

**fgets**()的参数是字符串名和读取的字符数，以及一个指向你想从哪里读取字符串的指针。**stdin**意味着从**标准输入**，也就是从键盘上读取。

**gets**和**fgets**之间的另一个区别是，换行符`\n`**fgets**会存储。
content.text_html:
The fgets() arguments are the string name, the number of characters to read, and a pointer to where you want to read the string from. stdin means to read from the standard input, which is the keyboard. Another difference between **gets **and **fgets **is that the newline character is stored by fgets.

content.text: **fgets**()只从**stdin**中读取**n-1**个字符，因为必须为`\0`留出空间。
content.text_html:
fgets() reads only n-1 characters from stdin because there must be room for '\0'.

fgets()只从stdin中读取n-1个字符，因为必须为'0'留出空间。
